• The sentence is also a negative sentence. 
 
• Negatives in the simple past are formed by adding didn't (informal) or did not (formal) before the simple form of the verb.
 
• The verb BE is an exception to this; in the case of BE, we just add n't (informal) or not (formal) after "was" or "were".
 
• Thus, it is incorrect to use the **past tense watched **in the sentence instead of the simple verb form **watch.**
 
• So, **option 1 **is the correct answer. 

**So the correct sentence is-** *We were not able to watch the movie due to lockdown.*

questions.question:

The Registrar informed the candidate that the last date ______ submission of forms was over.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'for'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given blank needs a **preposition** to indicate the duration of the time of submission.
 
• The **preposition at ** is used to indicate precise time - ***at ****3'o clock*
 
• The preposition for is used as a function word to indicate the duration of time or extent of space - *gone **for **two days*
 
• The preposition to is used as a function word to indicate position or relation in time - *five minutes **to **ten*
 
• The preposition in is used for months, years, and longer periods of time - ***in **May*
 
• Thus, **for **is the most appropriate preposition for the given blank, making **option 2 **the correct answer.

**So the correct sentence is-** *The Registrar informed the candidate that the last date** for** submission of forms was over.*

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 3 ∶ 5 ∶ 7 and their LCM is 840. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the terms in a **ratio** are co-prime, then **HCF** = LCM ÷ (Product of ratio terms).

Ratio terms are 3, 5, and 7 (all are **prime numbers**, hence co-prime).

⇒ HCF = 840 ÷ (3 × 5 × 7)

⇒ HCF = 840 ÷ 105 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of three numbers = 3 : 5 : 7 and **LCM** = 840.

Let the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** be x.

⇒ The three numbers are 3x, 5x, and 7x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d785c42400c71566ab799804dfa69afee115090118d762960b5f3d7a818e43d.png] 

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of 3x, 5x, and 7x is calculated as:

⇒ LCM = x × LCM(3, 5, 7)

Since 3, 5, and 7 have no common factors other than 1:

⇒ LCM(3, 5, 7) = 3 × 5 × 7 = 105

⇒ Total LCM = 105 × x

According to the question:

⇒ 105x = 840

⇒ x = 840 ÷ 105

⇒ x = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF × LCM.

HCF of Ratios

If three numbers are in the ratio a : b : c and their HCF is H, then the numbers are Ha, Hb, and Hc. Their LCM will be H × LCM(a, b, c).

Co-prime Numbers

A set of numbers is co-prime if their **HCF** is 1. For co-prime numbers, their **LCM** is simply the product of the numbers.</p

questions.question: An article was sold for Rs.1,190 after allowing a discount of 15%. If 12.5% discount is given, then for how much should it be sold?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **Selling Price (SP₁)** = Rs. 1,190 at 15% discount.

Ratio of SP₁ to SP₂ based on discounts = (100 − 15) : (100 − 12.5) = 85 : 87.5.

85 units = Rs. 1,190 ⇒ 1 unit = 1,190 ÷ 85 = 14.

New Selling Price (SP₂) = 87.5 × 14 = Rs. 1,225.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formulas:** MP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − D%) | New SP = MP × (100 − New D%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/442916032c738aa6e26e382a2db38b2d06007e29c16e7e6d021ade0f40ba9c18.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = Rs. 1,190, **Discount** = 15%.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 1,190 × 100 ÷ (100 − 15) = 1,190 × 100 ÷ 85.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 14 × 100 = Rs. 1,400.

⇒ New **Discount** = 12.5%.

⇒ New **Selling Price** = 1,400 × (100 − 12.5) ÷ 100 = 1,400 × 87.5 ÷ 100.

⇒ New **Selling Price** = 14 × 87.5 = Rs. 1,225.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

Effective Ratio

When the **Marked Price** remains constant, the ratio of two different Selling Prices is directly proportional to the multipliers of their respective discounts: SP₁/SP₂ = (100 − D₁%)/(100 − D₂%).</p

questions.question: A 144-m-long wire of radius 4 mm is melted to form a sphere. What is the surface area (in cm²) of the sphere, assuming there is no wastage of material?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert units to **cm**: **Radius** (r) = 0.4 cm, **Length** (L) = 14400 cm.

**Volume of wire** = π × (0.4)² × 14400 = 2304π cm³.

Set **Volume of Sphere** equal to wire volume: 4/3 × π × R³ = 2304π.

⇒ R³ = 1728 ⇒ **Radius of sphere** (R) = 12 cm.

**Surface Area** = 4 × π × (12)² = 576π cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 576 π cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** of the wire (L) = 144 m = 144 × 100 = 14400 cm

**Radius** of the wire (r) = 4 mm = 4/10 = 0.4 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Volume of Cylinder** = π × r² × L

**Volume of Sphere** = 4/3 × π × R³

**Surface Area of Sphere** = 4 × π × R²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8120c3ffdaea84b8793376a8cb0de7fc1ad2fe811afcd7b9620ec66647f8b069.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Volume of the wire** = π × (0.4)² × 14400

⇒ **Volume of the wire** = π × 0.16 × 14400 = 2304π cm³

Since the wire is melted to form a **sphere**, their volumes are equal:

⇒ 4/3 × π × R³ = 2304π

⇒ 4/3 × R³ = 2304

⇒ R³ = (2304 × 3) ÷ 4

⇒ R³ = 576 × 3 = 1728

⇒ R = √³1728 = 12 cm

Now, calculating the **surface area of the sphere**:

⇒ **Surface Area** = 4 × π × (12)²

⇒ **Surface Area** = 4 × π × 144 = 576π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 576 π cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When one solid object is melted and recast into another shape, the **Total Volume** remains constant, provided there is no wastage.

Sphere Properties

For a sphere of radius R, the **Volume** is 4/3 × πR³ and the **Total Surface Area** is 4πR².

Cylinder Properties

A wire is essentially a thin **Cylinder**. Its volume is calculated as πr²h, where r is the radius and h is the length.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure all dimensions are in the same unit before calculation. 1 m = 100 cm and 1 cm = 10 mm.</p

questions.question: 'A' alone can complete a work for Rs. 6,500 in 15 days. With the help of 'B', the work is completed in 12 days. The share of 'B' is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Days taken: **A** = 15 days, **(A + B)** = 12 days.

Total Work (LCM of 15, 12) = **60 units**.

Efficiency: **A** = 60 ÷ 15 = 4; **A + B** = 60 ÷ 12 = 5.

Efficiency of **B** = 5 − 4 = 1.

Share of **B** = (Efficiency of B ÷ Total Efficiency) × Total Wages = (1 ÷ 5) × 6,500 = **Rs. 1,300**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total amount for the work = **Rs. 6,500**, Time taken by **A** = 15 days, Time taken by **A and B** together = 12 days.

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = (Combined Efficiency) − (Efficiency of A) = 5 − 4 = 1

⇒ Ratio of efficiency **A : B** = 4 : 1

⇒ Share of **B** = (Efficiency of B ÷ Total Efficiency) × Total Wages

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the **ratio of work done** by the individuals, which is also the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the same duration.

questions.question: By which British statute were Indian representatives, for the first time, allocated seats for election in Indian Legislative Councils?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Indian Councils Act, 1892.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Councils Act 1892 brought the provision of bringing additional members into the Legislative Council through indirect election**. For the first time, the element of an election was introduced into the Indian political system. Provisions of the 1892 act.
 
• The act increased the number of additional or non-official members in the legislative councils as follows:
 
 
• In 1892, out of 24 members, only 5 were Indians.
 
• The members were given the right to ask questions on the budget (which was barred in the Indian Councils Act 1861) or matters of public interest but had to give notice of 6 days for it.
 
• They could not ask supplementary questions.
 
• The principle of representation was initiated through this act. The district boards, universities, municipalities, chambers of commerce, and zamindars were authorized to recommend members to the provincial councils.
 
• The legislative councils were empowered to make new laws and repeal old laws with the permission of the Governor-General.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Indian Council Act, 1861:**

 
 
• For the executive functions of the Council, a fifth member was added. Now there were five members for home, military, law, revenue, and finance.
 
• Lord Canning, who was the Governor-General and Viceroy at the time, introduced the portfolio system. In this system, each member was assigned a portfolio of a particular department.
 
• Lord Canning nominated three Indians to the Council in 1862 namely, the Raja of Benares, the Maharaja of Patiala, and Sir Dinkar Rao.
 
• Any bill related to public revenue or debt, military, religion, or foreign affairs could not be passed without the Governor-General's assent.
 
• The Viceroy had the power to overrule the council if necessary.
 
• This Act restored the legislative powers of the Governor-in-Councils of the Presidencies of Madras and Bombay (which were taken away by the Charter Act of 1833).
 
 
 
• **The Charter Act of 1833:**
 
 
• The Governor-General and his Council were given vast powers.
 
• The Council got full powers regarding revenue, and a single budget for the country was prepared by the Governor-General.
 
• For the first time, the Governor-General's Government was known as the 'Government of India' and his Council as the 'Indian Council'.
 
• The Governor-General of Bengal was to be the Governor-General of India.
 
• All powers, administrative and financial, were handed over to Governor-General in Council.
 
• A Law Commission under Lord Macaulay was constituted for the codification of laws

• **Chlorine **elements can be used to treat/purify water.
 
• **Chlorination** is one of many methods that can be used to disinfect water.
 
• It is a chemical disinfection method that uses various types of chlorine or chlorine-containing substances for the oxidation and disinfection of what will be the potable water source.
 
• **Chlorine inactivates a microorganism by damaging its cell membrane. Once the cell membrane is weakened, chlorine can enter the cell and disrupt cell respiration and DNA activity.**
 
• The main objective of this chlorine addition is to disinfect the water and maintain chlorine residuals that will remain in the water as it travels through the distribution system.
 
• Any type of chlorine that is added to water during the treatment process will result in the formation of hypochlorous acid (HOCI) and hypochlorite ions (OCI-), which are the main disinfecting compounds in chlorinated water.
 
• The amount of chlorine that is required to disinfect water is dependent on the impurities in the water that needs to be treated.
 
• Chlorination is able to provide a residual to reduce the chance of pathogen regrowth in water storage tanks or within the water distribution system.
 
• Chlorination has been proven to be very effective against bacteria and viruses.
 
• However, it cannot disinfect all waterborne pathogens. Certain pathogens, namely protozoan cysts, are resistant to the effects of chlorine.

questions.question: Who discovered the TB vaccine?

__
 
• **Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccine was developed by French bacteriologists Leon Calmette and Camille Guerin in 1921. It is used for the Prevention of Tuberculosis.**
 
• The vaccine provides protection against** meningitis, leprosy, non-invasive bladder cancers, and disseminated TB** in children.
 
• A recent study has shown that the countries which have BCG vaccination in their immunization program have a low rate of death due to COVID-19.
 
• Tuberculosis (TB) disease is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Tuberculosis (TB) usually attacks the lungs.
 
• BCG vaccine was first considered by the WHO Expert Committee on Biological Standardization in its thirteenth report.
 
• BCG vaccine is one of the most widely used of all current vaccines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Edward Jenner** - Edward Jenner, FRS FRCPE was a British physician and scientist who pioneered the concept of vaccines including creating the smallpox vaccine, the world's first ever vaccine. The terms vaccine and vaccination are derived from **Variolae vaccinae**, the term devised by Jenner to denote **cowpox**.

 
 
• **Jonas Salk** - Jonas Edward Salk was an American virologist and medical researcher who developed one of the** first successful polio vaccines.**
 
 
 
• **Louis Pasteur** - He pioneered the study of **molecular asymmetry**; discovered that microorganisms cause **fermentation **and disease; originated the process of **pasteurization**; saved the beer, wine, and silk industries in France; and developed vaccines against **anthrax **and **rabies**.
 
• 
 
**Robert Koch**, a German physician and one of the main founders of modern bacteriology, made significant contributions to our understanding of tuberculosis.

 
On March 24, 1882, Koch announced the** discovery of the bacterium that causes tuberculosis, **known as Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This was a significant breakthrough because TB was one of the deadliest diseases of Koch's time, responsible for a high number of deaths, particularly in crowded, impoverished, urban areas.
